subject: Finalizing DPA language — training carve-outs, subprocessors & DocuSign
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-medical.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-medical.com, legal@acme-counsel.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Final DPA language — training/use of Customer Data

Neha — thanks for taking this across the line. We're almost ready to sign, but legal needs one last confirmation on the training carve-out and data transfer controls before procurement can execute. High-level asks from our counsel: 

1) A clear ban on using Customer Data to train or improve models (both internal and external model variants) unless we provide explicit, written opt-in.
2) Definitions that separate "Customer Data" (raw content) from telemetry and aggregate metrics; telemetry may be allowed for service stability only if anonymized.
3) Confirmation of legal basis for EU transfers (SCCs or equivalent) and a current subprocessors list.

We attached Acme counsel's preferred language as a reference. Can Redwood confirm acceptance or propose final redlines? If acceptable, procurement will sign via DocuSign and share the envelope. We need to get this done by EOD Friday to meet project timelines.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Head of IT Security & Privacy
Acme Medical

--
Attachment: Acme_Counsel_requested_DPA_clauses.pdf (pdf)

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-medical.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Final DPA language — training/use of Customer Data

Emily — appreciate the clear asks. Quick summary of where we stand and proposed final language: 

- Redwood position (high level): We will NOT use Customer Data (defined below) to train or improve our models or any third-party models without Customer's prior written consent. We are comfortable allowing limited, anonymized operational telemetry for service stability and performance tuning (e.g., latency histograms, error rates) that cannot be traced back to an individual Customer.

- Proposed definition (extract for DPA): 
  "Customer Data" means all data, content, and information that Customer or its End Users submit to the Services, excluding aggregated and de-identified usage metrics that cannot reasonably be re-identified. 

- Proposed carve-out clause (to add to Section 4 Data Use): 
  "Provider will not use Customer Data to develop, train, or improve Provider's machine learning models or any models provided to other customers, except with Customer's prior written consent. Provider may collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry solely for the operation, monitoring, and improvement of the Service, provided such telemetry cannot be re-identified to Customer or End Users."

- On transfers: We will execute the EU SCCs and provide our Subprocessors list (attached). If you need Data Processing Agreement + SCCs executed, we can push via DocuSign today.

I am cc'ing Dev for a short technical confirmation and Evelyn for legal confirmation. If that language looks good, I'll prepare the final DPA bundle and send the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Nikhil
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf)

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Final DPA language — training/use of Customer Data (technical note)

Looping in a couple of technical specifics Emily's counsel will likely probe: 

- Telemetry/metrics: We capture request-level logs for debugging (short TTL), and we capture aggregate metrics. We can implement a filter to drop or aggregate any fields that might be PII/PHI for Acme. TTL for request logs can be set to 30 days (by default 90) for Dedicated customers; we can make 30 days contractual if needed.

- Subprocessors & transfers: Our current EU-path: primary processing happens in AWS eu-west-1 or GCP europe-west1 depending on customer region; we rely on SCCs for transfers from EU to US control plane. Subprocessors list attached — includes cloud providers + CDN + monitoring vendor. We can commit to 30 days' notice before adding a new subprocessor and to honor reasonable mitigation steps (i.e., additional DPA terms or suspension of processing) if a subprocessor change is problematic.

- Model training: From the runtime perspective, we do not perform offline training on customer content in hosted accounts and do not share customer content with third-party model vendors. If Acme requires an on-prem or private deployment, we can provide a VPC/on-prem package which avoids our model training pipelines entirely.

I'll attach the Subprocessors list and a short technical FAQ for the legal team.

—Dev
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Subprocessors_List_Q1_2026.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: Technical_FAQ_for_DPA.pdf (pdf)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-medical.com>, legal@acme-counsel.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Final DPA language — training/use of Customer Data

Emily — thanks for the input. From a legal POV the proposed language below is acceptable to Redwood and aligns with industry best practice. A few legal clarifications we included in the redline: 

• Clarified "prior written consent" can be provided via an executed DPA or documented email from an authorized signatory.
• Added explicit examples of permissible "aggregated, de-identified telemetry" (e.g., CPU utilization percentiles, API error counts) and excluded any content-level examples.
• Added a subprocessor notice period: 30 days except for emergency security-critical subprocessors (we will provide notice as soon as practicable in those cases).

Proposed final sentence to close the loop: 
  "For the avoidance of doubt, Provider shall not use Customer Data to create, refine, or otherwise improve any machine learning model or algorithm outside the scope of the Services without Customer's prior written consent; aggregated and de-identified metrics for service health are excluded from this restriction."

If Acme is good with that, Redwood can prepare the DPA + SCCs as a single DocuSign package. I will review the DocuSign envelope before it goes out.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--

Please send the DocuSign envelope and include the SCCs — procurement will countersign. If possible, please include a visible line item on the DocuSign for the DPA and a separate line item for the SCCs.

Best,
Emily
